lines.trans: Emergency bulletin from the station desk: our mapmaker arrives at three sharp today!
Three in the afternoon?! Ziad, turn both ovens up to baking heat this second!
Both switches on! How fast can four berry-and-almond cakes bake and cool, Salma?
Forty minutes in the oven, thirty minutes to cool, ten minutes for warm honey glaze!
That brings us to twenty-five past two—with thirty-five minutes to spare!
I will grease all four round tins with butter while you whisk the eggs, Salma!
Nour, rinse those four bowls of fresh summer berries and pat them dry with linen!
Rinsing fast and gently! Thank goodness we tested all three glazes on Sunday!
Imagine serving Batch One brass polish or Batch Two roof tiles at three today!
Less joking and faster whisking, Ziad—fold the ground almonds in smoothly!
Wait—do you hear Tariq calling my name from the lobby? Something happened with the room keys!
Go save the front desk, Nour; Ziad and I own this kitchen until half past two!

See you soon!

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنقذ, بينقذ).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
You saved my whole trip.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: The typical Jordanian form of شي: في إشي؟ 'is something wrong?', ولا إشي 'nothing at all'.

examples.text: في إشي بدك إياه من السوق؟
examples.trans: Is there anything you want from the market?
Nothing happened at all, relax.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing one woman.

examples.trans: You must be Nour!
You are today's heroine, Nour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: First working day of the Jordanian week (pronounced il-ahad).

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنرتب جدول الأسبوع كله.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we plan the schedule for the whole week.

examples.text: المدارس والمكاتب بعمان بتفتح يوم الأحد.
examples.trans: Schools and offices in Amman open on Sunday.

meanings.note: Form VII passive of خبز ('to bake'): describes bread or pastries baking in the oven.

examples.text: الكعكة بتحتاج ربع ساعة لتنخبز منيح.
examples.trans: The cake needs a quarter of an hour to bake properly.
The bread was baked this morning and is still warm.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.
We arrived at nine o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Core Levantine word for 'want', inflected with pronoun suffixes rather than verb prefixes.

examples.trans: What do you want to do now?
I wanted to talk with you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for stone, ceramic, or courtyard tiles; single tile is بلاطة.

examples.trans: We wiped the courtyard tiles with water this morning.

examples.text: بلاط المطبخ بارد على الرجلين بالشتاء.
examples.trans: The kitchen tile is cold on the feet in winter.

meanings.note: Collective plural بيض ('eggs'), singulative بيضة ('one egg'), dual بيضتين ('two eggs').

examples.trans: I fried two eggs for breakfast.
Hot eggs are delicious with bread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of برّد (to cool down).

examples.text: حط الصينية على شبك التبريد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Put the tin on the cooling rack for ten minutes.
The cooling room keeps the fruit fresh.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تجارب.

examples.trans: The trial week went by fast.
It was a very sweet experience.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتخيل, بيتخيل).

examples.trans: Imagine how the whole story started!
I never imagined finding the train here.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: From ح-ر-ر ('hot, warm'); describes warmth retained by clay cups or weather temperature.

examples.text: الفخار السميك بيحفظ حرارة الشاي وقت طويل.
examples.trans: Thick pottery holds the heat of the tea for a long time.
The oven temperature is ideal for morning bread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; الحمد لله means 'thank goodness'.

examples.trans: Thank goodness everything is fine!
We arrived safely, thank goodness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخبار.

examples.trans: I have good news for you today!
They have no news yet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Culinary verb for whisking eggs, lemon curd, or cream until smooth.

examples.text: نور بتخفق البيض مع الليمون والسكر بهدوء.
examples.trans: Nour whisks the eggs gently with lemon and sugar.

examples.text: خفقت سلمى الكريمة حتى صارت ناعمة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: Salma whisked the curd until it turned smooth and glossy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخفف, بيخفف).

examples.text: الخشب بيخفف الصدى عن حجر الشارع.
examples.trans: The wood softens the echo off the street stone.
We dimmed the light in the courtyard in the evening.

meanings.note: Feminine instance noun from خلط ('to mix'): a spice blend, pastry glaze, or sauce mix.

examples.trans: We prepared the sugar and lemon glaze for the cake.

examples.text: كل بيت عنده خلطة بهارات خاصة.
examples.trans: Every home has its own special spice blend.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخلص, بيخلص).

examples.trans: I finished making the bed quickly!

examples.text: كل ما أخلص عزف كنا نحكي.
examples.trans: Whenever I finished playing, we used to chat.

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دهانات.

examples.trans: Room eight has fresh paint.

examples.text: ريحة الدهان راحت لما فتحنا الشباك.
examples.trans: The smell of paint cleared when we opened the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday word for butter. Metaphorically means 'the essence' or 'bottom line'.

examples.text: بدي خبز سخن مع شوية زبدة.
examples.trans: I would like warm bread with a little butter.
Is this salted butter or unsalted?

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian/Levantine household word for a ceramic or glass soup/breakfast bowl (plural زبادي).

examples.text: حطت سلمى الزيتون بزبدية فخار بيضا.
examples.trans: Salma put the olives in a white ceramic bowl.

examples.text: ع الطاولة أربع زبادي صغار للمربى.
examples.trans: On the table sit four small bowls for jam.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Active participle of سمع ('to hear'), standard in Jordanian for 'can you hear?' (سامعني؟).

examples.trans: I hear you clearly on the phone.
Do you hear the sound of a car outside the gate?

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشغل, بيشغل).

examples.trans: Can we turn the water heater on now?
She started up the coffee machine in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian spelling/pronunciation (duhur) for midday (12:00 p.m.).

examples.text: الكافيه بيقدم شوربة سخنة من الضهر للمسا.
examples.trans: The café serves hot soup from noon until evening.

examples.text: الشمس بتكون عالية ودافية وقت الضهر.
examples.trans: The sun is high and warm at noon.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Masculine noun used for sugar glaze on pastries as well as paint or enamel on surfaces.

examples.text: طلاء السكر بيعطي لمعان حلو للمعجنات.
examples.trans: The sugar glaze gives a nice shine to the pastries.
We painted the door with a fresh white coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Active participle from عجل ('to hurry'): used for urgent dispatches, news, and calls.

examples.text: وصلنا خبر عاجل من مكتب المحطة.
examples.trans: Urgent news reached us from the station office.
There is an urgent call from the manager.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: The standalone number ten.

examples.trans: You arrived ten minutes early.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Wash dishes, clothes, windows or your hands.

examples.trans: I washed the cups and put them on the shelf.
Wash your hands before eating.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: The primary interrogative word for quantity, price, or duration in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدم, بيقدم).

examples.trans: We serve fresh breakfast every morning.
She served the guests mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Masculine material noun used both for woven linen fabric and flax/linen twine.

examples.text: هاد المريول مصنوع من قماش الكتان البارد.
examples.trans: This apron is made from cool linen fabric.
Linen holds up well in summer and its heat.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Masculine abstract noun (distinct from the verb لطف 'to soften'). Used for kind manners and gentle handling.

examples.text: الضيافة باللطف والابتسامة أحلى ما يكون.
examples.trans: Hospitality with kindness and a smile is the nicest thing.
Thank you for your kindness and help today.

meanings.note: Active participle indicating the ongoing state of gripping or grasping something.

examples.trans: I am holding the torch steady!
He was holding a blue suitcase in his hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مدورة, plural: مدورين).

examples.trans: Where should I hang the round mirror?
We put a round wooden table in the corner.

meanings.note: Form III verbal noun from مزح ('to joke'): lighthearted teasing or playful banter.

examples.trans: No joking now—the matter is serious.
Friendly banter makes the atmosphere relaxed.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Used for things like coffee, spices, or meat.

examples.trans: I want freshly ground coffee.

examples.text: ضفنا نص معلقة هيل مطحون ناعم عالقهوة.
examples.trans: We added half a spoonful of finely ground cardamom to the coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Used for both a workplace (office) and the piece of furniture (desk).

examples.trans: The keys are on the reception desk.
The wooden desk under the window is wide.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنادي, بينادي).

examples.trans: Do we call each other by first name here?
Salma called everyone to breakfast.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Form II transitive counterpart of نشف ('to become dry'): used for drying berries, dishes, or towels.

examples.text: اغسل التوت ونشفه منيح بفوطة نضيفة.
examples.trans: Wash the berries and dry them well with a clean towel.

examples.text: نشفي إيديكي قبل ما تفتحي الدفتر.
examples.trans: Dry your hands before opening the notebook.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Feminine abstract noun from ناعم ('soft/smooth'). Common phrase: بنعومة ('gently / softly').

examples.trans: The lanterns sway gently with the breeze.

examples.text: مسكت الفرشاية بنعومة عشان ما تسيح الألوان.
examples.trans: I held the brush gently so the colours wouldn't run.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوصل, بيوصل).

examples.trans: Our guest arrived right on the second!
An official letter arrived at noon.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
